sections.label: Three aims of legislative changes
sections.summary: The passage states three aims: making legislative provisions clearer, updating them with revised terminology and definitions, and streamlining operational effectiveness and policy delivery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: First, making legislative provisions clearer; second, updating legislative provisions in light of revised terminology and definitions; and third, streamlining and improving operational effectiveness and delivery of our policies.

sections.label: Splitting protected performances offence
sections.summary: It splits the offence under section 450(2) of the CA into two offences: one for live performances and one for recordings of performances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Second, it splits the offence on causing protected performances to be seen or heard in public, under the current section 450(2) of the CA, into two separate offences: one, in relation to live performances and another in relation to recordings of performances.

sections.label: Updating juvenile definition in CPC
sections.summary: Clause 4(a) and (b) update the definition of a juvenile in section 2(1) of the CPC to a person 10 years or older but below 18.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: First, clause 4(a) and (b) update the definition of a "juvenile" in section 2(1) of the CPC to refer to a person who is 10 years of age or older, but below 18 years of age.

sections.label: Extending secured creditor notification period
sections.summary: The amendment to section 327(4)(a) of the IRDA extends the period for a secured creditor to notify the Official Assignee of intention to claim interest from 30 to 60 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The second amendment is to section 327(4)(a) of the IRDA, to extend the period within which a secured creditor has to notify the Official Assignee of the secured creditor's intention to claim interest on the secured debt, from 30 days after a bankruptcy order is made against the debtor to 60 days.

sections.label: Waiving costs owed to Director
sections.summary: The proposed amendment to section 16 of the LAAA provides that costs owed by an aided person to the Director of Legal Aid may be waived partially or completely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Third, the proposed amendment to section 16 of the LAAA will provide that costs owed by an aided person to the Director of Legal Aid, in connection with that aided person's application for legal aid, may be waived either partially or completely.

sections.label: Pawnbrokers as excluded moneylenders
sections.summary: It clarifies that all pawnbrokers regulated under the Pawnbrokers Act 2015 are excluded moneylenders for the purposes of the MLA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: First, it clarifies that all pawnbrokers regulated under the Pawnbrokers Act 2015, or PBA, are "excluded moneylenders" for the purposes of the MLA.

sections.label: FIN as identification alternative
sections.summary: The amendment to section 2(1) of the PBA allows an individual's FIN to be used instead of their foreign passport number for identification.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The second amendment is to section 2(1) of the PBA, to allow the use of an individual's foreign identification number, or "FIN", as an alternative to their foreign passport number, for identification purposes.

sections.label: Revising subsidiary legislation in batches
sections.summary: Clause 12(e) allows subsidiary legislation to be revised in batches, and clauses 12(e) and 12(i) give LRCs discretion not to revise certain types.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As at 26 June 2024, there are about 4,900 pieces of subsidiary legislation under around 349 Acts to be revised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Given the sheer volume, the amendment in clause 12(e) is needed to allow subsidiary legislation to be revised in batches, rather than on a single date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The amendments by clauses 12(e) and 12(i) also give the LRCs discretion not to revise certain types of subsidiary legislation, for instance, subsidiary legislation that applies to certain time periods.

sections.label: Women's Charter child access orders
sections.summary: Clause 13 makes a drafting adjustment to section 126B so the child access enforcement measures apply to all access orders under section 126.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 13 amends the Women's Charter to make a minor drafting adjustment to the new section 126B, which was inserted by section 35 of the Women's Charter (Amendment) Act 2022 and is yet to be commenced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The amendment clarifies that the new measures to enhance the enforcement of child access orders apply to all access orders made under section 126 of the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The definition of "juvenile" has been amended from referring to someone between the ages of seven and 16 to refer to a person who is between the ages of 10 and 18.

sections.label: Youth Courts jurisdiction raised
sections.summary: In 2019 Parliament passed amendments to the CYPA raising the Youth Courts' jurisdiction to include youth offenders aged 16 and 17.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2019, Parliament passed amendments to the CYPA to raise the jurisdiction of the Youth Courts to hear cases involving youth offenders to include those aged 16 and 17.

sections.label: MSF to announce operationalisation date
sections.summary: MSF has been working with relevant agencies and will announce the operationalisation date of the 2019 CYPA amendments later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) has been working on this with the relevant agencies and will announce the operationalisation date of the relevant amendments from the CYPA of 2019 later this year.

sections.label: Clarification on announcement timing
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Minister of State said MSF would announce the effective date later this year, not that the provisions would be effective this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Speaker, just a clarification on what the Minister of State just said.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: He mentioned that MSF would announce later this year when the provisions will be effective, and not that the provisions will be effective by this year, right?
